title: LabRepair: a repair proposal is not an approval token

scenes.title: Why a handover matters
scenes.shot: Show the NEBIUS-009 heading and replay boundary; keep OFFLINE visible.
scenes.narration: An analysis can run successfully and still support the wrong conclusion. LabRepair gives reviewers a reproducible handover instead of another confident explanation. This prototype shows what was checked, what was rejected, and what has not run.

scenes.title: Inspect an untrusted proposal
scenes.shot: Show the normal ledger.py diff and its reviewed-literal, synthetic label. Do not stage or run it.
scenes.narration: Here is a fixed, synthetic invoice fixture. Only ledger dot py is editable as a proposal; the cases and runner are protected. The reviewed literal response suggests removing duplicate invoices. It is not output from a live NVIDIA model, and we do not execute its candidate code.

scenes.title: A plausible diff is not approval
scenes.shot: Expand the exact source/request bindings, then show BLOCKED and both missing gate reasons.
scenes.narration: Source, request and policy hashes bind this diff to one exact workspace. A fresh local replay reproduces the saved decision: blocked. We have not verified an isolated backend or an enforceable spending limit. A plausible patch is therefore a reviewable proposal, not a tested or approved repair.

scenes.title: A refusal is a product result
scenes.shot: Show protected-change REJECTED; switch to qa/rejected.html generated from the rehashed forged verdict. Label the negative control.
scenes.narration: Now the negative control tries to change the protected runner. It is rejected. A separate bundle forges an accepted verdict and recomputes its checksum. Independent replay still refuses it, and the failure page contains no successful result or download links. A checksum cannot grant authorization.

scenes.title: Do not rewrite the original science
scenes.shot: Return to Original science, separate record: 2.61 versus 1.9625, BLOCK and NOT_ESTABLISHED. Do not imply the invoice fixture repairs this case.
scenes.narration: The scientific record stays separate. In the existing synthetic Maya case, the submitted S value is two point six one; registered replay is one point nine six two five. The original claim remains blocked. Fixing invoice code cannot validate a Bell claim, and this is not a hardware experiment.

scenes.title: A replayable handover, with honest limits
scenes.shot: Show the three fixed JSON download links and NOT_RUN/unknown metrics. Use local files if the browser transfer remains unverified.
scenes.narration: The three downloads preserve the offline bundle, fresh replay and historical context. The planned NVIDIA on Nebius integration still requires verified model access, covered credits, a monetary cap and real isolation. Real inference and isolated execution have not run. Our current deliverable is evidence another reviewer can inspect and replay without trusting model prose.

limits: All inputs are synthetic; invoice proposals are independent from original Bell/CHSH science.
The NVIDIA response is a reviewed literal fixture, not live model output.
No provider transport, candidate execution, isolated runtime or hardware test is demonstrated.
Checksums detect changes, not authenticated identity.
The planned 165-second timeline is not a recorded-video duration.
This draft does not satisfy missing mandatory sponsor integration; no eligibility/registration/submission claim is made.
Source/UI observations are historical NEBIUS-009 evidence; no fresh provider or browser-transfer result is implied.
